comment: A rungler is a shift register clocked by one oscillator and fed its data bits by the other, with the three newest bits read as a three-bit converter, so it steps between eight levels. Rungler 1 moves oscillator A and rungler 2 moves oscillator B, and their sum moves both filter peaks. The filter's audio input is the comparator square of the two triangles. A third modulation stream comes from a sample-and-hold of oscillator A latched by oscillator B. The structure follows olaf's SuperCollider realisation of the Blippoo Box, reimplemented in C++, and Hordijk's own 2009 Leonardo Music Journal paper is cited. The panel prints bulla, freq a, freq b, res, b>a, a>b, sh>osc, r>a, r>b, sh>flt, peak 1, peak 2, r>flt, a, b, p1, p2, rung and out.
